items.title: Sol Yaged interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000
items.q: we became very good friends. I brought you some pictures of he and I together... I’m indebted to him quite a lot because he’s done a lot for me.

ctx.x: Yeah. Tell me about getting hooked up with Steve Allen.

I was working at a place right before The Metropole, Monk, at a place called The Somerset Hotel on 47th Street off Seventh Avenue. The Metropole was on 48th and Seventh Avenue. I was there with a trio. And he used to come in every night to sit in with me, Steve Allen. This was before he had a show. He had just come to New York from Chicago, and we used to let him sit in with us all the time. And we became very good friends. I brought you some pictures of he and I together when we made the Benny Goodman picture.…
Right. Was he a good student?

items.title: Steve Allen interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999
items.q: Sol was the perfect choice, and a very easy guy to work with, so he gave me several weeks of just basic lessons

ctx.x: I understand Sol Yaged came out and gave you some —

Yeah. As soon as I agreed to do the movie then of course the question was even though I was a musician I knew nothing about the clarinet, so we had to hire somebody to teach me, and somebody knew about Sol, our mutual friend Bobby Rosengarden once said something hysterically funny, he described Sol Yaged as quote the Jewish Benny Goodman. For you young people, Benny himself is Jewish. But anyway Sol was the perfect choice, and a very easy guy to work with, so he gave me several weeks of just basic lessons, you…

Benny Goodman lived in a fog. He was Mr. Absent Minded and often didn’t know what he was doing. He’d walk on stage with his fly open and stuff. And through accident, he was just a careless man and didn’t think much about the world. He was just the greatest clarinet player of them all. So just after the movie, NBC and Universal Studios got together to do a little promotion going in both directions, so that meant booking Benny on our show, which was on the air Sunday nights at NBC at the time. So Benny himself…
